source: Cost to a US payer of one acute cardiovascular event in the SELECT composite — cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction or non-fatal stroke. Built as an incidence-weighted blend of published US inpatient costs for acute myocardial infarction and for ischaemic stroke, both of which cluster in the $20,000-25,000 range for the index admission. Tier B: the component costs are published, the weighting across event types in this composite is the analyst's.

American Diabetes Association, Economic Costs of Diabetes in the U.S. in 2022: $12,022 in excess annual medical expenditure attributable to diabetes per person with diagnosed diabetes. This is an annual cost of a prevalent case, applied here as the cost carried by one avoided incident case in the year it would have arisen — a conservative reading, since a case avoided this year would have carried that cost again in every year after.

AHRQ Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project: the mean cost of a US inpatient stay is approximately $14,100. An all-cause average rather than a condition-specific one, which is why it is tier B — an obesity-related admission is not necessarily an average admission.
Published US estimates of the annual incremental medical expenditure attributable to hypertension put it near $1,900 per patient per year. Applied as the annual cost of one avoided incident case.

Analyst construction: the annual incremental cost of escalated obstructive sleep apnoea management — device therapy, titration studies and specialist review — in the US. Assembled from list prices for the components rather than taken from a single published estimate, and tiered C accordingly.
